title: Ben Duckett intent on retaining England Test place and prioritises Notts over IPL
content:
Ben Duckett turned his back on the Indian Premier League (IPL) to ensure he does everything he can to retain his England place after the crushing disappointment of the Test team’s heavy Ashes defeat.

Duckett withdrew from his $211,000 (£159,000) deal with Delhi Capitals just days before he was due to return to India — the new 2026 IPL tournament begins on Saturday — preferring instead to prioritise red-ball cricket with Nottinghamshire.

The left-handed opener will now potentially have six County Championship matches to attempt to score enough runs to preserve his place at the top of the England order when they face New Zealand at Lord’s in the first of three Tests on June 4.

“I wasn’t proud of how things went in Australia,” Duckett told reporters, including The Athletic, at the Nottinghamshire media day at Trent Bridge on Friday. “But I’ve been good during my career in acknowledging when I’ve got it wrong and hopefully, moving forward, people will see how much playing for England means.

“For me pulling out of the IPL, turning down a good chunk of money and missing the opportunity to play with and against some of the best players in the world to be here playing for Notts is a step in the right direction to show how important playing for England is. I think everyone else will back that up in their own way.”

Duckett was one of England’s biggest disappointments in Australia, making just 202 runs at an average of 20.20 with his highest score of only 42 coming in his final innings in Sydney. While he featured in the national team’s white-ball tour of Sri Lanka, he was unused in the subsequent T20 World Cup, where England were eliminated by India in the semi-finals.

The 31-year-old also became an emblem of the issues England had off the field in Australia when a video emerged of him appearing inebriated in Noosa during England’s infamous break after the second Test when they were already 2-0 down in the Ashes.

That left him in danger of losing his place, with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) admitting some of their players behaved unprofessionally in Australia and insisting they will take greater notice of performances in county cricket when they make their first Test selection.

“I’ve held my hands up since then,” said Duckett, who has accepted he will now be banned from playing in the IPL for the next two years because of his late withdrawal, of the Noosa incident.

“It’s not something any professional sportsman should be doing. We were having a break that was planned before the series and if we were winning it probably wouldn’t have been news and nobody would have cared.

“If it had been Travis Head (the prolific Australian batter) in that video, people are probably loving it and that’s sport. We were struggling as a side and I was struggling as a player so I shouldn’t have put myself in a position like that. That goes for any human being, let alone a professional sportsman.

“The video came out just before the Melbourne Test and that was a really tough period for me. it certainly wasn’t the best Christmas I’ve had in my life but the one thing I can take is the support I had from the ECB.

“They could have not been more supportive of me at a tough moment in a big series. It was not what they needed and I thank Keysy,(managing director Rob Key), Baz (coach Brendon McCullum) and Stokesey (captain Ben Stokes) for all their support.

“I genuinely don’t know whether I’ll be in the England team for the first Test, but I’ll do everything I can over the next four or five weeks to be in the best shape of my life. I can’t promise I’ll average 75 for Notts in these games, but I’ll be giving it my all to try to get to the best place I can and see where we go from there.”
